analysis.title: Natixis Institutional Outlook Survey 2027: Welcome to the machine
key_insights: Survey of 515 institutional investors in 29 countries (CoreData, Sept-Oct 2026): 67% say AI can drive markets for the next 20 years, and 80% say AI still has a long runway for growth.
71% worry a CapEx slowdown could upend 2027 economic growth, and 70% worry AI will not deliver all the productivity gains already priced in. The 71% reaches 84% in APAC.

Foreword says the November 5 Nasdaq sell-off (-5.5% in one day, 10% below its October high) came two days after Democrats won the House and Senate. The survey reads it as fear of AI regulation and data center development.

63% globally and 70% in the US worry local pushback on data centers will threaten the AI buildout. 77% expect AI backlash to force government responses, and 67% expect AI regulation to add effective guardrails.
73% are bullish on stocks, led by defense stocks (77%). 56% remain bullish on Mag 7 stocks, but 49% say the Mag 7 will perform like the 'Meh 7' in 2027.

66% expect equity volatility to rise. Average probability of a global 10% to <20% correction is 38%, and of a 20%+ crash is 19%. 54% expect higher return dispersion, and only 27% expect correlation to rise.

Information technology is the top sector pick (61.2% outperform), then healthcare (59%) and financials (51.1%). Real estate is the most bearish (52% expect underperformance), and consumer discretionary is next at 35%.
Inflation: G20 inflation rose from 3.4% in 2025 to 4.0% in 2026 on commodity and energy costs. 40% expect further increases in 2027 and 39% expect no change. 49% expect higher energy prices.
Rates view is split: 37% expect rates to rise, 32% to fall, 31% no change. 54% expect only one or two cuts in their local market, 23% none, 11% three or more, and 12% expect hikes.

54% are bullish on bonds (North America only 35%). 58% expect long duration to outperform short, and 52% are lengthening duration. 41% expect bond volatility to rise and 51% expect corporate defaults to rise.

Top economic threats: government debt/fiscal crisis (45%), geopolitical shock (37%), geopolitical fragmentation (37%), tech bubble (34%), AI-related disruptions (27%). Government borrowing was $17T in 2025 and is expected to reach $18T in 2026, with 80% of borrowing used to refinance existing debt.

Top geopolitical threats: US-China competition (43%), broadening military conflicts (43%), cybersecurity (36%), tariffs and non-tariff barriers (31%), energy security (31%). 66% say the global economy is splitting into East and West spheres.

China: 60% expect China to keep struggling to regain growth, and 75% call slow growth China's new normal. World Bank puts China growth at 4.4% in 2026 and 4.3% in 2027. 77% say cheap AI is China's greatest economic weapon, but only 43% think China will eclipse the US in AI technology.
Emerging markets: 47% plan to raise EM equity allocations, and 63% (72% in APAC) cite dollar weakness as the best EM opportunity in years. 51% expect India to become the top EM for investment.

Equity allocation plans: 48% will increase Asia-Pacific, 47% emerging markets, 41% Europe, and only 33% US equities (28% plan to decrease). In North America US equities is the only class with more decreases (32%) than increases (21%). In the UK 56% plan to cut US exposure.
Fixed income allocations favor quality. 44% will increase investment-grade corporates and 44% green bonds. High-yield is the weakest call at 24% increasing against 25% decreasing.

Alternatives: 72% expect a 60:20:20 alts-diversified portfolio to beat 60:40. 56% plan to add infrastructure, 51% private debt, 49% private equity/venture. 70% say private markets offer higher return potential than public markets.
Infrastructure's share of the alternatives sleeve is projected to rise from 15.6% to 17.5%. Data centers are the top nontraditional real estate opportunity (67%).

Crypto: 73% are bearish on the asset class. 30% plan to increase crypto allocations against 13% decreasing. Only 46% see crypto as a legitimate institutional investment and 24% currently invest in it. 55% say an unwinding of crypto treasury funds could deliver a major shock to prices.
Commercial real estate is the most bearish asset call (75% bearish) and residential real estate is 52% bearish.

Active management: 71% say conditions favor active management in 2027 and 64% expect active to outperform passive. 57% already use active ETFs and 37% more plan to. 74% say active management is essential in fixed income.

AI adoption and employment: 98% of institutional investors use AI in their job. 75% say replacing junior roles disrupts the talent pipeline, and 49% say AI-driven layoffs will make them rethink how they define recession.

sector_views.rationale: 61.2% of surveyed institutions expect outperformance, on AI CapEx demand across infrastructure, software and platforms.
59% expect outperformance, citing innovation (GLP-1, gene therapy) and lower economic sensitivity from aging-population demand.
35% expect underperformance as higher prices, rates and unemployment weigh on consumer spending.
52% expect underperformance on persistent inflation and higher-for-longer rates. 56% are bullish on nontraditional real estate such as data centers and logistics.
77% are bullish on defense stocks, and 73% expect higher defense spending to support growth in developed markets.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Global disinflation that ran 36+ months was disrupted in 2026 by commodity and energy costs, so there is no relief expected in 2027.
The OECD says 80% ($13.5T) of borrowing refinances existing debt, which raises fiscal crisis concern.
The survey treats slow growth as China's new normal.

macro_indicators.indicator: Rate cuts expected in local market in 2027 (survey)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Institutions are not counting on many cuts, and sticky inflation limits the room to ease.
Cited by the survey as context for bubble concern (34% worry tech is approaching bubble status).

macro_indicators.indicator: AI CapEx at Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft
macro_indicators.interpretation: 63% of institutions expect continued spending to drive 2027 growth.

crypto_views: 73% of institutions are bearish on cryptocurrency for 2027.
30% plan to increase crypto allocations and 13% plan to decrease. EMEA is 41% vs 13% and North America 19% vs 3%. Latin America is 9% vs 36%.
46% consider crypto a legitimate institutional investment and 24% currently invest in it.
79% say crypto is inappropriate for most retail investors, and 65% say AI hype has distracted from the case for crypto.
55% believe the unwinding of crypto treasury funds could deliver a major shock to prices.
Binance engineer laptop malware attack attributed to a suspected North Korean unit, with more than $6 billion taken.
risk_factors: Government debt and fiscal crisis (45% top threat).
CapEx slowdown upending growth (71%) and AI productivity gains not matching what is priced in (70%).
Local pushback on data centers and AI regulation threatening the AI buildout (63%).
A significant new AI technology development raising equity concentration risk (73%).
Persistent inflation (55%) and interest rates (49%) as the biggest portfolio risks.
Rising corporate defaults (51%) and bond volatility (41%).
Cybersecurity (36%), with cybercrime growing from about $3T in 2020 to $10T in 2025.
charts_described: Sector picks chart: information technology 61.2% outperform, healthcare 59%, financials 51.1%, energy 48.9%, real estate 52.4% underperform per text.
Odds of correction/crash chart: global 10% to <20% correction at 38% and 20%+ crash at 19%.
vol_and_positioning: 66% expect equity volatility to rise in 2027 (Latin America 73%, APAC 71%, EMEA 69%, North America 55%).
Average probability of a 10% to <20% global correction is 38%, and of a 20%+ crash is 19%.
54% expect dispersion to increase, 27% expect correlation to rise, 44% no change, 30% a decline.
41% expect bond volatility to rise. 61% expect currency volatility to increase.
44% of current active-ETF investors increase their active-ETF exposure when volatility rises.
The foreword says the Nasdaq fell 5.5% on November 5, taking it 10% below its October high. The survey also cites an October 30 sell-off that wiped out $1 trillion in tech value in one day.
geopolitical: US action in Venezuela, followed by war with Iran, and the unresolved Russia-Ukraine war, with the Iran war's effect on world oil supplies cited.
US-China competition and a split of the global economy into East and West spheres (66%).
Tensions in the South China Sea seen as a more immediate market threat by 58%.
Disputes over new frontiers such as space and the Arctic (63% expect more conflict).
Rare earths security called the new energy security by 68%.
US tariffs plus protectionist measures by China, the EU and India (subsidies, export controls).
A suspected North Korean cybercrime unit netted more than $6 billion through a malware attack tied to an engineer's laptop at Binance.

tension_points.bull_case: 80% say AI has a long runway for growth, 63% expect continued spending to drive 2027 growth, and 69% expect productivity gains to show up in market growth.
tension_points.bear_case: 71% say a CapEx slowdown could upend growth, 70% worry productivity gains are not all delivered but already priced in, and 63% fear data center pushback.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A slowdown or deceleration in AI CapEx spending by companies that do not find the anticipated payoffs.

tension_points.bull_case: 56% remain bullish on Mag 7 stocks and 61% rank information technology as the best sector.
tension_points.bear_case: 49% expect the Mag 7 to perform like the Meh 7, and 73% worry a new AI technology development could expose concentration risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued Mag 7 lag against the index would force the 'hard lessons about concentration risk' 61% warn of.

theme_stances.key_argument: Institutions see AI as the growth engine for 2027 but worry a CapEx slowdown or unmet productivity gains could break it.
theme_stances.evidence: AI remains the throughline on growth

theme_stances.evidence: Mag 7 will perform more like the Meh 7
